description.narrative: Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities. Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the Grant Obligations and Conditions, the obligatory dates for submission of the annual/additional reports are mentioned. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

actual.value:
Twenty participants were trained within the programme, from five different TVETs (CFPA El Alia, CFPAF Rimel, CFPAF Ben Arous, CFPAF Zerkine, CFPAF Manouba) and two agricultural institutes (INPFCA and Synagri).
The programme offered them both cultivation knowledge and skills as new educational and communicational skills, as an entrepreneurial mindset.
To foster experimental learning, demonstration fields, a demo greenhouse and a demo raft system were established. On the demonstration field at El Alia and the raft system, multiple brassicas were cultivated. On a saline plot of a nearby farmer different varieties of red beets were cultivated. Additionally, in the demonstration greenhouse tomatoes were cultivated.
Next to that, also visits were made to the demonstration greenhouse at CSFPA Chott Mariem (established in the prior TMT project led by Delphy), the Dutch greenhouse company Rainbow Horticulture and the post-harvest company SODEA, to extend and strengthen the connections of the participants.
During the last training week on entrepreneurship, also multiple entrepreneurs were invited to stimulate the entrepreneurial mindset of the participants. This was strengthened by the Entrepreneurship Workshop Day, hosted by our consortium, together with two other Dutch TMT+ consortia. During this day, each TMT+ presented their programme and one of the participants pitched their lessons learnt. Each consortia provided a concise part of their entrepreneurship training, after which mixed groups were made to discuss their lessons learnt, ways to implement and transfer the gained knowledge and how to foster collaboration between the institutions.
All and all, the programme provided a lot of knowledge and expertise on cultivation, education and entrepreneurship, plus made and strengthened a lot of connections between agricultural individuals, (knowledge) institutions and companies.

comment.narrative: 27-10-2022: Next to five TVETs, also two participants of the agricultural institutes INPFCA and Synagri were trained. Moreover, throughout the training programme many representatives of regional and national agricultural institutes have joined for one or multiple days. As mentioned above, the participants from the TVETs will train and already have trained students, farmers and growers. INPFCA is involved in every Tunisian TVET, overseeing the pedagogical part of education. The trained participant from the INPFCA will be able to share the gained knowledge and skills with her colleagues, and with time to all Tunisian TVETs. Moreover, also the three private sector companies and institutes that were visited benefit from the knowledge and expertise shared during the visits. It is hard to quantify the exact amount but the total reach is estimated to be 330 beneficiaries, based on the following estimation: - Around 5 other staff members, 10 farmers and 50 students per TVET (25 staff members, 50 farmers & 250 students) - Around 12 farmers trained and advised by Synagri - Two private sector companies and one other TVET which were visited - Ten representatives of regional and national agricultural institutes
